blocks.text: Imagine you need to efficiently manage a dynamic list of tasks, always prioritizing the most urgent one. How can we structure this list to quickly access and update priorities?

blocks.markdown: A binary heap is a complete binary tree that satisfies the heap property. It is commonly used to implement priority queues, where the most urgent task can be accessed and managed efficiently.

blocks.title: Heap Property
blocks.text: In a min-heap, for any given node $i$, the value of $i$ is less than or equal to the values of its children. In a max-heap, the value of $i$ is greater than or equal to the values of its children.

blocks.markdown: Binary heaps are typically implemented using arrays. The key advantage of using an array is the efficient indexing scheme that allows us to navigate the tree structure without using pointers.

blocks.title: Array Indexing Scheme
blocks.text: For a node at index $i$, its parent is at index $\lfloor \frac{i-1}{2} \rfloor$, the left child is at index $2i + 1$, and the right child is at index $2i + 2$.

blocks.title: Verify the Heap Property
blocks.prompt: Given the array [3, 9, 5, 12, 15], verify if it satisfies the min-heap property.

steps.text: Identify the parent-child relationships using the array indexing scheme.
Check each parent node to ensure it is less than or equal to its children.
For index 0 (value 3), children are indices 1 (value 9) and 2 (value 5).
For index 1 (value 9), children are indices 3 (value 12) and 4 (value 15).
For index 2 (value 5), there are no children since the array ends.

blocks.answer: The array [3, 9, 5, 12, 15] satisfies the min-heap property.

blocks.markdown: Insertion into a binary heap involves adding the new element at the end of the array and then 'sifting up' to restore the heap property.

blocks.title: Insert into a Binary Heap
blocks.prompt: Insert the value 4 into the min-heap represented by the array [3, 9, 5, 12, 15].

steps.text: Add 4 to the end of the array: [3, 9, 5, 12, 15, 4].
Sift up: Compare 4 with its parent at index 2 (value 5).
Now, 4 is at index 2, with parent at index 0 (value 3).
Since 4 > 3, no more sifting is needed.

blocks.markdown: Extracting the minimum element from a min-heap involves removing the root and then 'sifting down' to restore the heap property.

blocks.caption: Time complexities of binary heap operations.

points: Binary heaps are complete binary trees that satisfy the heap property.
They are efficiently implemented using arrays with a specific indexing scheme.
Insertion and extraction operations maintain the heap property through sifting.
